title: Expand direct one-batch DuckDB-to-Parquet migration for daily_basic to include 2025
instructions: Read .kiro/agents/direct-period-duckdb-migration-loop.md and .kiro/specs/direct-period-duckdb-migration/requirements.md first. Expand migration coverage from daily_basic/2026-only to daily_basic/2025-01-01 <= trade_date < 2027-01-01 (2025 + 2026 combined) in one end-to-end batch. The production router (query-entry-router.mjs) only supports a single contiguous window per pointer, so this must widen the window rather than stack a second manifest, matching the precedent already used to grow the pilot (2026-05) into the full 2026 year. Use C:/Workspace/Quanttrading/Quanttrading/data/quant.duckdb only with OPEN_READONLY. Preserve a rollback snapshot of the current metadata/query-entry/daily_basic.json pointer (the accepted task-029 lineage, most recently refreshed) before any switch. Execute the already validated playbook: inventory (expect roughly 1.56M rows for the combined window), contract alignment check, staged Parquet write for the combined window, clean-version-manifest/v1 generation under partition_id period=2025-2026, source-vs-target consistency verification in the same real DuckDB engine (row count, date range, duplicate keys, bidirectional EXCEPT, ordered row checksum, null profile, provenance distribution), atomic pointer publish (temp+fsync when supported+rename), routed smoke (boundary/before/after/invalid/missing cases plus full/window/outside-window counts vs source), AND an explicit freshness smoke comparing routed vs source row counts for the most recent trade dates. Roll back to the saved pointer state if any check fails. Do not write source DuckDB, do not drop/archive, do not change ingestion, do not touch the router module (already generalized, no code changes needed). Produce a complete execution JSON+MD artifact recording every step, then finish with finish-task using --agent claude so Codex can independently review. IMPORTANT coordination rule learned from the prior refresh episode: do not perform this task's production pointer switch more than once, and if a duplicate/competing task or process is discovered touching the same pointer, stop and let only the first-claimed task perform the write.
